thread:
maria: heads-up — ran a quick staging sweep of the paged-KV allocator change. seeing a ~12% p99 latency regression for short requests (seq <= 256) after the block-table fallback kicks in.

kai: can you paste the profiler output? which stage is spiking — kernel or memcpy?

maria: attaching the trimmed profiler snapshot:
```
# top hotspots (sample counts)
1) attention_kernel_fused (gpu0): 42% total
2) kv_page_alloc (gpu0): 18% total (lots of small allocations)
3) memcpy_async (gpu0->host): 9%
4) scheduler_batch_mux: 6%
```

maria: also saw this in the kernel selection log: `selected_kernel=flash2_paged fallback=flash_blocked` for many short seqs. the fallback path is inflating latency.

sam: hmm. that suggests allocator fragmentation + extra kernel prep cost. current allocator behavior: try to allocate exact number of blocks, else fall back to single large block per head which then triggers the blocked attention codepath. maybe we should change strategy to pre-split a reserved slab into fixed-size blocks for small seqs.

lee: agreed. proposal: maintain two pools per device: small-block pool (for up to 256 tokens, block_size=64) and large-block pool (for >256). allocator tries small pool first, else large. keeps block-table lookups O(1).

kai: any numbers if we simulate that?

maria: quick sim with a prototype allocator:
```
workload: 90% short (seq<=128), 10% long (seq>1024)
baseline (current): p50=22ms p99=120ms tokens/s=980
patched (dual-pool): p50=20ms p99=106ms tokens/s=1120
```

sam: nice. that regains most perf. what about memory overhead? pre-splitting costs ~4% extra GPU RAM at peak in our sim.

lee: tradeoff seems fine. Also need to avoid excessive metadata size for block-table; we can compress entries (store 32-bit offsets instead of 64-bit) and pack per-shard tables. expected table overhead <1% memory.

maria: another angle — kernel selection: flash2 is faster for short contiguous KV but our paged layout fragments contiguity. If we can expose a "contig hint" to the selector when small-block pool hits, selector can prefer the fused_paged kernel variant optimized for small-block contiguity.

kai: do we have a fused_paged variant ready? I thought eng-runtime had a microkernel for that but not fully tuned.

sam: there's a WIP branch with a fused_paged kernel tuned for block_size=64; needs register tiling adjustments. I can rebase and run benchmarks.

maria: please run comparisons against flash2 and fused_blocked. request: bs=8, concurrency=4, seqs=[64,128,512,2048]. include p50/p95/p99 and tokens/s. command we used: `./bench --model=m-llama2 --kernels=all --bs=8 --concurrency=4 --seqs=64,128,512,2048`

lee: one more perf regression we saw — batching heuristics: when short+long mix entrails, scheduler merged a long request into a batch that previously would have been immediate, raising tail latencies. consider two-pass batching: prefilter by seq-length buckets then batch within bucket with a time cap.

kai: yes, bucketed batching + priority for latency-sensitive short buckets. time cap default 8ms for short, 20ms for long.

maria: sounding good. I'll do a staged rollout: allocator dual-pool + block-table compression + bucketed batching. deploy-bot: starting canary on staging (canary=10% devices).

deploy-bot: deploy started — canary devices: gpu-12,gpu-19,gpu-21. artifact: paged-kv-v2.

maria: if canary looks good I'll roll to 50% tomorrow. watch p99 on /generate and kernel selector logs for `contig_hint` usage. tagging @kai @sam @lee — thanks. :rocket:
